newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Press Digest - Ireland - January 14.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Ireland - January 14.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.

- The validity of thousands of district court proceedings in a number of places over the last two-and-a-half years has been left open to challenge after the Attorney General said some courts were not properly constituted.

- The Irish Farmers' Association on Monday expressed outrage at a 5 pence per pound drop in the price paid for cattle at meat factories as efforts continued to reopen the Egyptian market for live cattle.
- Reductions in payroll costs for business and a special package for farmers will constitute an important part of next week's Irish budget.
- A major political row was brewing last night after it emerged that the Blood Transfusion Service Board manufactured the anti-D blood product for 14 years without obtaining the necessary licences.
- Ireland had the fastest growing tourist industry in the world over the past decade, Tourist Board director general Matt McNulty said on Monday.
- Agriculture minister Ivan Yates is unlikely to meet the Egyptian veterinary delegation due to arrive in Ireland on Wednesday to hear Ireland's case for lifting the ban on live cattle shipments.

- The opposition Progressive Democrats on Monday stepped up pressure on the government in advance of next week's Irish budget by calling for two percent reductions in both the 48 percent and 27 percent tax rates.
